Why is energy needed to remove an electron from a gaseous atom?

options.A: The electron is attracted to the other electrons in the atom.
options.B: The negative electron is attracted to the positive nucleus.
options.C: The negative electron is repelled by the positive nucleus.

stem: Which change would increase the attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron of an atom?

options.B: More protons in the nucleus with the outer electron in the same shell.
options.C: Adding an extra inner shell of electrons.
options.D: The outer electron moving to a shell further from the nucleus.

stem: Which statement about the first ionisation energy of an atom is correct?

options.A: It depends only on the number of protons in the nucleus.
options.B: It depends on the strength of attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron.
options.C: It depends on how strongly the outer electron is attracted to the inner electrons.
options.D: It depends only on the number of electrons in the outer shell.

stem: The first ionisation energy of oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen. Which statement explains this?

options.A: Oxygen has more shielding by inner shells than nitrogen.
options.B: Two of the oxygen 2p electrons are paired in one orbital, and the repulsion between them makes one easier to remove.
options.C: Oxygen has a lower nuclear charge than nitrogen.
options.D: The half-filled 2p subshell in nitrogen is more stable, so it has a lower energy.

stem: The first ionisation energy of sodium is much lower than that of neon. Which statement explains this?

options.A: The outer electron in sodium is in a $2p$ orbital.
options.B: The outer electron of sodium is in a new shell further from the nucleus and is shielded by more inner electrons.
options.C: Sodium has a greater nuclear charge than neon.
options.D: The atomic radius of sodium is smaller than that of neon.
